correctness.rationale: The affine substitution u=2a+1, v=2b+1 preserves Haar measure, and the factor 64 is a square unit. The only possible singular zero classes of F=(u²−1)(v²−1)+64n would require n=0 or 1+64n=0 modulo p. On a smooth zero ball, varying the coordinate with unit derivative gives an affine bijection for each next residue digit of F/p; this establishes uniformity and square probability 1/(2(p+1)) by summing the even positive valuations and square units. The measure of F=0 is zero. Summing the quadratic character in v gives 1+p χ(n)(3+χ(m)), with the exceptions u=±1 and u²=m accounted for separately. At F=0 the substitution w=(u²−1)v gives w²=(u²−1)(u²−m); the quartic has simple roots and two rational points at infinity, and its affine points with u=±1 are exactly the two points to remove. Thus Z=p−3−a_p. Substitution yields the claimed formula; Hasse gives the stated uniform remainder. Independently checked both examples and 420 generic prime-power cases using weighted triangular residues in the original coordinates and the exact residual smooth-ball mass.
